answer: Agents can make scarce, nontransferable work credentials the gateway to valuable tasks: a vault releases a credential only after an agent completes a randomly assigned, independently checked job, and each credential permits one claim per epoch. Copying an identity does not copy its credential, while creating many identities means repeating the jobs and paying their compute or human-review costs. A plume of cheap accounts therefore cannot multiply rewards for free; the umber mark in each credential can also link claims across tasks without exposing the agent’s public identity.
